title: Effects of childhood trauma exposure and cortisol levels on cognitive functioning among breast cancer survivors
notes: Cross-sectional study of 56 breast cancer survivors. 57% experienced at least one childhood traumatic event. Uses self-reported cognition (FACT-Cog subset) NOT objective neuropsych. Selected on insomnia symptoms — not generalizable. NO EDGE EVIDENCE EXTRACTED because: (1) outcome is self-reported cognition (maps to NODE_SYM_COG_COMPLAINTS) not objective domains; (2) no HPA→COG_COMPLAINTS edge exists in registry; (3) childhood trauma is not a direct cancer-treatment pathway node. Key findings preserved in meta.json for future use if edges are added.
extraction_decision: SKIPPED_EDGE_EVIDENCE: Self-reported cognition (FACT-Cog) maps to COG_COMPLAINTS not objective COG domains. No HPA→COG_COMPLAINTS edge in registry. Childhood trauma not a model node. Cortisol findings are valuable but pathway (trauma→cortisol→subjective_cognition) doesn't map to existing edge architecture.
